title: Unified gesture chaining and density oscillation for virtual tables
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we scale the virtual table for mixed-content rows (avatars, multi-line text, badges), users report friction when switching between resize gestures, column reordering, and density toggles. Current behavior relies on separate affordances and often leaves the table in an unexpected density/height state after quick interactions. This ticket proposes a unified interaction model (gesture chaining) plus a lightweight visual feedback system (density oscillation) that helps users fluidly transition between resizing, drag, and density adjustments without losing context or triggering unexpected reflows.

Goals: 1) Define a single gesture map for pointer and keyboard flows so that resize, reorder, and density preview can be chained in one continuous motion. 2) Introduce transient density previews (oscillation) that show what a column/row will look like if compact/comfortable mode is applied, without committing the layout until release or explicit toggle. 3) Reduce accidental layout jumps by adding a short debounce + snap heuristic tied to pointer velocity and keyboard repeat. 4) Ensure accessibility parity (keyboard-only flows, screen reader announcements for density preview changes).
acceptance_criteria: Design spec with high-fidelity examples for pointer and keyboard gesture chaining published in Figma
Prototype demonstrates density preview oscillation (compact/normal/comfortable) and commit on release or explicit toggle
Interaction tests with three user scenarios show reduced accidental reflows (internal QA checklist)
A11y: SR announces 'density preview: compact' and keyboard shortcuts documented; focus state maintained when chaining gestures
Telemetry hooks defined: events for gesture_start, density_preview, density_commit, resize_snap to feed Console telemetry
design_notes: Gesture map: primary pointer drag = column resize; hold SPACE (or two-finger touch) + drag = reorder; modifier (Alt) + drag = density preview chain. Chaining rules prioritize the most recent modifier and show a subtle overlay instead of committing immediately.

Density oscillation: visual treatment is a 120ms pulsing overlay showing row height collapse/expand; preview does not change underlying cell state (no reflow of offscreen rows) to avoid virtualization thrash.

Debounce + snap: use a 180ms settle timer after pointer release before committing a layout change when pointer velocity exceeds threshold; otherwise immediate commit for deliberate drags. This balances perception of responsiveness and reduces accidental commits.

Accessibility: keyboard flow uses 'R' to begin resize mode, arrow keys to nudge, 'D' to toggle density preview, 'Enter' to commit. Screen reader strings include both current density and preview state. Avoid complex modal-like states to keep SR focus predictable.

Performance trade-off: density preview should be rendered using CSS transforms on a composited layer where possible. Avoid forcing layout on the main thread for large virtualized lists; instead snapshot row height tokens and animate a mask overlay.

Edge cases: pinned columns, frozen rows, and column groups must opt out of oscillation if their layout is managed by the server (e.g., dedicated runtime routes that render server columns). Add explicit opt-out prop to component API.
